subject.title: [Feature]: Move away from useMultiFileAuthState for Baileys

question: Which SQLite owner and security/upgrade contract should be authoritative for bundled WhatsApp credentials and Signal keys?
rationale: Repository policy requires SQLite and one canonical migration owner, but consolidating cryptographic state requires maintainer approval of database placement, permissions, transaction boundaries, backup and rollback behavior, verification, and legacy cleanup.

options.title: Shared state plugin schema
options.body: Use WhatsApp-owned Kysely tables or plugin KV in `state/openclaw.sqlite`, with strict filesystem permissions and a doctor migration that verifies complete state before deleting legacy files.

options.title: Dedicated WhatsApp database
options.body: Use a dedicated SQLite database only if measured schema, volume, locking, backup, or lifecycle requirements demonstrably do not fit the shared state database.

options.title: Continue file hardening
options.body: Retain Baileys multi-file authentication and continue targeted recovery work, accepting that the upstream production-store recommendation remains unresolved.

recommendation.title: Shared state plugin schema
recommendation.body: Use WhatsApp-owned Kysely tables or plugin KV in `state/openclaw.sqlite`, with strict filesystem permissions and a doctor migration that verifies complete state before deleting legacy files.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest focused history is the existing WhatsApp credential persistence, recovery, and safety implementation that this migration would replace or extend.
